question.text: A ball of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math>, moving with a velocity of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>, collides with a spring of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>8</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> and force constant <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The length of the compressed spring is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo mathvariant="italic"> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math>, to the nearest integer, is ___ .

solution.text:
Let's say the compression in the spring by:y. So, by work-energy theorem we have

⇒12mv2=12ky2⇒y=mk·v⇒y=4100×10⇒y=2 m

⇒ Final length of spring,=8-2=6 m.
